We want to make it easier for you to talk regularly with the people you care about. We want you to build genuine relationships with your friends and communities close to home or around the world. Original, reliable, playful, and relatable. These are the values that connect our users and our employees at Discord.", COMPANY_REBRAND_HISTORY_BEGINNING_TITLE: "Prologue", COMPANY_REBRAND_HISTORY_BEGINNING: "Discord was started to solve a big problem: how to communicate with friends around the world while playing games online. Since childhood, founders Jason Citron and Stan Vishnevskiy both shared a love of video games, cherishing the friendships and connections that formed while playing them. At the time, all the tools built for this job were slow, unreliable, and complex. Jason and Stan knew they could make a better service that encouraged talking, helped form memories, and recreated the feeling of togetherness all found through gaming.", COMPANY_REBRAND_HISTORY_START_TITLE: "Chapter One", COMPANY_REBRAND_HISTORY_START: "So, in 2015, Stan and Jason started to bring Discord to life. People from all over the world loved it. Discord made it easy to genuinely communicate with friends, going beyond casual talking. Friends were staying in touch with their various communities. Discord was making it easy to participate in conversation, hopping around text, voice and video to talk. The technology was complex but the goal was simple: make Discord an inviting and comfortable home to jump into with your communities and friends. Within a few years, Discord began to take off, and devoted people who loved our product sprung up around the world.", COMPANY_REBRAND_HISTORY_TODAY_TITLE_2: "Where are we now?", COMPANY_REBRAND_HISTORY_TODAY: "Discord is used by everyone from local hiking clubs, to art communities, to study groups. Discord has millions of people creating places for their friends and communities, talking for upwards of 4 hours per day on the platform. Discord is now where the world talks, hangs out, and builds relationships. Discord lets anyone create a space to find belonging—just like it did for Jason and Stan.", COMPANY_REBRAND_METRICS_TITLE: "Our metrics", COMPANY_REBRAND_OFFICES: "Our office", COMPANY_REBRAND_HIRING_HEADING: "Come make some Discord with us", COMPANY_REBRAND_HIRING_BUTTON_2: "Open Jobs", COMPANY_REBRAND_HIRING_TEXT_2: "Become part of a group of passionate people passionately crafting exceptional products they’re passionate about. This is done in Discord under your Server Settings.", PARTNERS_APPLY_STEP_ENGAGEMENT_LABEL: "Step 2", PARTNERS_APPLY_STEP_ENGAGEMENT_TEXT: "Once you’ve set your server to Community, you should see a Partner Program tab. So, what’s next?", PARTNERS_APPLY_WHATS_NEXT_SUBTITLE: "While Partnership is not guaranteed, we’d love to hear from you. If you’ve followed the steps above, apply within Discord under the Partner Program tab and we’ll get back to you as fast as bureaucracy will let us. Remember, it’s not just about the numbers. We take an overall look at your community. Acceptance is based on both quantitative and qualitative factors, and may vary from one candidate to the next.", PARTNERS_FEATURED_TITLE: "Meet our Partners", PARTNERS_FEATURED_SUBTITLE: "Whether you’re a community about learning how to cook, a server about fantasy sports, fans of your favorite game, or anything in between, we support engaged communities and content creators.", PARTNERS_FEATURED_SPECTRUM_DESCRIPTION: "Relationships & Identity, General Chatting", PARTNERS_FEATURED_AP_STUDENTS_DESCRIPTION: "Education", PARTNERS_FEATURED_BNANS_DESCRIPTION: "Gaming, Content Creator", PARTNERS_FAQ_QUESTION_1: "What do you look for in Partners?", PARTNERS_FAQ_ANSWER_1_1: "Someone who appreciates me for who I am and likes long walks on the beaches and candle-lit dinners and... wait, I think I misread the question.", PARTNERS_FAQ_ANSWER_1_2: "Really, we look for thriving communities and content creators that show an authentic enthusiasm for Discord. We want to support communities that support us. Numbers on other platforms don’t always represent a engaged Discord community, so we don’t require specific, non-Discord related numbers like views or followers. Acceptance as a Partner is based on your server. More details on what we use to determine acceptance be found above or in our [Help Center article](https://support.discord.com/hc/articles/115001494012). However, meeting these requirements does not guarantee acceptance. Acceptance is based on both quantitative and qualitative factors, and will vary from one candidate to the next.", PARTNERS_FAQ_QUESTION_2: "What numbers do I have to hit as a community to be accepted into the Partner Program?", PARTNERS_FAQ_ANSWER_2: "Numbers on other platforms don’t always represent an active Discord community, so we no longer require non-Discord related numbers like views or followers on other platforms. Instead, acceptance as a Partner is based on your server. Details on what we use to determine acceptance be found in our [Help Center article](https://support.discord.com/hc/articles/115001494012).", PARTNERS_FAQ_QUESTION_3: "What perks does my community get from this?", PARTNERS_FAQ_ANSWER_3: "Aside from the perks listed above, your server will also get a better bitrate, which is fancy talk for your voice channels will sound better. As such, we encourage everyone to participate in our open bug bounty program, which incentivizes researchers and hackers alike to responsibly find, disclose, and help us resolve security vulnerabilities. Thanks for participating and happy bug hunting!", SECURITY_APPROACH_TITLE: "How we approach security issues", SECURITY_APPROACH_LINE_1: "Discord will not take legal action against users for disclosing vulnerabilities as instructed here.", SECURITY_APPROACH_LINE_2: "Vulnerability reports will always be responded to as fast as possible—usually within 24 hours.", SECURITY_APPROACH_LINE_3: "Based on the validity, severity, and scope of each issue, we'll reward you with awesome shtuff (or just cold, hard cash if you prefer).", SECURITY_RULES_TITLE: "Program Rules", SECURITY_RULES_LINE_1: "Only use and test on accounts and servers you directly own. Testing should never affect other users.", SECURITY_RULES_LINE_2: "Testing should be limited to sites and services that Discord directly operates. We will not accept reports for third-party services or providers that integrate with Discord through our APIs.", SECURITY_RULES_LINE_3: "Don't perform any actions that could harm the reliability or integrity of our services and data. Some examples of harmful activities that are not permitted under this bounty include: brute forcing, denial of service (DoS), spamming, timing attacks, etc.", SECURITY_RULES_LINE_4: "Don't use scanners or automated tools to find vulnerabilities.", SECURITY_RULES_LINE_5: "No information about issues found should be publicly disclosed or shared until we've completed our investigation and resolution. Once the internal solution is in place, we will update the policy and communicate the re-allowance.", SECURITY_REPORT_PROCESSING_TITLE: "Processing Report Submissions", SECURITY_REPORT_PROCESSING_LINE_1: "We offer rewards for issues which are submitted and resolved through Bugcrowd. If you have any questions about these Terms, please contact [privacy@discord.com](mailto:privacy@discord.com).\n\n Discord is made possible through the work of other [open source software](https://discord.com/acknowledgements).', COMMUNITY_GUIDELINES: "**Last Updated: May 19th, 2020.**\n\nWe created Discord to help people come together around games. It's been amazing to watch it grow into what it is today - a place where millions of diverse communities exist and people connect with old friends and new. We can't wait to see what's next.\n\nOur community guidelines are meant to explain what is and isn’t allowed on Discord, and ensure that everyone has a good experience. If you come across a message that appears to break these rules, please report it to us. We may take a number of steps, including issuing a warning, removing the content, or removing the accounts and/or servers responsible.\n\nThe overwhelming majority of people use Discord responsibly, so these guidelines may seem obvious. Still, we want to be clear about the expectations for our users. Every user of Discord should feel like their voice can be heard, but not at the expense of someone else.\n\n### Here are some rules for interacting with others:\n\n1. **Do not organize, participate in, or encourage harassment of others.** Disagreements happen and are normal, but continuous, repetitive, or severe negative comments may cross the line into harassment and are not okay.\n2. **Do not organize, promote, or coordinate servers around hate speech.** It’s unacceptable to attack a person or a community based on attributes such as their race, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, sexual orientation, religious affiliation, or disabilities.\n3. **Do not make threats of violence or threaten to harm others.** This includes indirect threats, as well as sharing or threatening to share someone’s private personal information (also known as doxxing).\n4. **Do not evade user blocks or server bans.** Do not send unwanted, repeated friend requests or messages, especially after they’ve made it clear they don’t want to talk to you anymore. Do not try to hide your identity in an attempt to contact someone who has blocked you, or otherwise circumvent the tools we have which enable users to protect themselves.\n5. **Do not send others viruses or malware**, attempt to phish others, or hack or DDoS them.\n\n### Here are some rules for content on Discord:\n\n6. **You must apply the NSFW label to channels if there is adult content in that channel.** Any content that cannot be placed in an age-gated channel, such as avatars, server banners, and invite splashes, may not contain adult content.\n7. **You may not sexualize minors in any way.** This includes sharing content or links which depict minors in a pornographic, sexually suggestive, or violent manner, and includes illustrated or digitally altered pornography that depicts minors (such as lolicon, shotacon, or cub). We report illegal content to the [National Center for Missing and Exploited Children](https://www.missingkids.org/gethelpnow/cybertipline).\n8. **You may not share sexually explicit content of other people without their consent**, or share or promote sharing of non-consensual intimate imagery (also known as revenge porn) in an attempt to shame or degrade someone.\n9. **You may not share content that glorifies or promotes suicide or self-harm**, including any encouragement to others to cut themselves, or embrace eating disorders such as anorexia or bulimia.\n10. **You may not share images of sadistic gore or animal cruelty.**\n11. **You may not use Discord for the organization, promotion, or support of violent extremism.**\n12. **You may not operate a server that sells or facilitates the sales of prohibited or potentially dangerous goods.** This includes firearms, ammunition, drugs, and controlled substances.\n13. **You may not promote, distribute, or provide access to content involving the hacking, cracking, or distribution of pirated software or stolen accounts.** This includes sharing or selling cheats or hacks that may negatively affect others in multiplayer games.\n14. In general, **you should not promote, encourage or engage in any illegal behavior.** This is very likely to get you kicked off Discord, and may get you reported to law enforcement.\n\n### Finally, we ask that you respect Discord itself:\n\n15. **You may not sell your account or your server.**\n16. **You may not use self-bots or user-bots to access Discord.**\n17. **You may not share content that violates anyone's intellectual property or other rights.**\n18. **You may not spam Discord**, especially our Customer Support and Trust & Safety teams. Making false and malicious reports, sending multiple reports about the same issue, or asking a group of users to all report the same content may lead to action being taken on your account.\n\n\nIf you see any activity that violates these guidelines, you can report it to us by filling out [this form](https://dis.gd/request).", LEGAL_EN_DISCLAIMER: "This translation is provided for information only. Learn more about our safety principles.", SAFETY_CATEGORY_LANDING_TITLE_NAVBAR: "Safety Center", SAFETY_LANDING_HERO_TITLE: "Discord Safety Center", SAFETY_LANDING_HERO_BODY: "Discord is a place designed for talking and hanging out with your communities and friends. Millions of diverse communities are on Discord including school clubs, gaming groups, art communities, and groups of friends spending time together.\n\nThe space for each community on Discord is called a server. Discord servers are invite-only places where you can talk, collaborate, and share. Conversations on servers are only with people you choose to talk to and about the topics you want to discuss. In this way and many others, Discord is not a traditional social media platform. There is no algorithm deciding what you should see. There’s no endless scrolling, no news feed, and no counting of likes.\n\nWe built this Safety Center to ensure that everyone feels comfortable and confident on Discord. We want to help you understand how we think about and prioritize safety, the policies we have in place, and how you can control your experience.", SAFETY_PRINCIPLES_TITLE: "Our Safety Principles", SAFETY_PRINCIPLES_BODY: "These principles guide us every day, ensuring Discord is always safe and secure for everyone.", SAFETY_PRINCIPLE_RESPONSIBILITY_TITLE: "With great power comes great responsibility.", SAFETY_PRINCIPLE_RESPONSIBILITY_SUBTITLE: "There’s a huge responsibility in being a place where millions of people talk to each other every day, and we want Discord to always be a welcoming place for you and your friends. We do not sell your data, nor do we share it with third parties for advertising purposes.", SAFETY_PRINCIPLE_CONTROL_TITLE: "We give you the tools to control your experience.", SAFETY_PRINCIPLE_CONTROL_SUBTITLE: "We’ve created tools for server owners to moderate their spaces. These tools allow you to enforce your rules and norms for your unique community. You can find out more about these tools here in the Safety Center.", SAFETY_PRINCIPLE_SAFETY_TITLE: "We take public safety very seriously.", SAFETY_PRINCIPLE_SAFETY_SUBTITLE: "We put your privacy first and as a rule do not scan or read your messages. However, we can do so for safety reasons. If an issue arises, we will investigate, review the situation, and take proper action. We know there are cases where bad actors are acting to cause violence or harm in the real world, and we make it clear to them that they don’t have a place on Discord.", SAFETY_PRINCIPLE_IDENTITY_TITLE: "Your identity is yours.", SAFETY_PRINCIPLE_IDENTITY_SUBTITLE: "Your account doesn’t have to be tied back to your real world identity — we want to make sure that everyone can be their true self and feel comfortable when they talk on Discord. But that **doesn’t** mean that someone can avoid consequences for their actions.", SAFETY_GUIDELINES_TITLE: "Our Community Guidelines", SAFETY_GUIDELINES_BODY: "We want Discord to be a safe, positive, and inclusive experience. For that to happen, we must all agree to a set of rules that guide our interactions on Discord.\n\nWhen you sign up to Discord, you agree to follow our [Community Guidelines]({guidelinesURL}) and refrain from behavior that isn’t allowed on the service. In exchange, it’s our job to make sure your experience is as amazing as it can be.\n\nWe have a zero-tolerance approach to anyone threatening other people with harm, sharing sexually explicit content of others without their consent, sharing content that glorifies or promotes self-harm, and illegal activities such as sharing child sexual abuse material. If you come across a message that appears to break these rules, you can report it to your server moderator or directly to us by [filling out this form]({reportFormURL}). We may take a number of steps including issuing a warning, removing the content, or removing the accounts and/or servers responsible.\n\n**For more information, please see the other parts of this Safety Center as well as our [Help Center]({helpCenterURL}).**", SAFETY_TABLE_OF_CONTENTS_HEADING: "Contents", SAFETY_REBRAND_LANDING_HERO_BODY: "Discord is a place dedicated to talking and hanging out with your friends, family and communities. Millions of diverse communities are on Discord, from small groups of old friends to huge servers where hundreds of thousands of people can connect over shared interests.\n\nDiscord isn’t a social media platform. There is no algorithm deciding what you should see, no endless scrolling, no news feed, no counting likes, no going viral. Instead, Discord is a place where everyone can be themselves and spend time with other people who share their interests and hobbies. Conversations on Discord are driven only by the people you choose and the topics you pick.", SAFETY_REBRAND_PRINCIPLES_TITLE: "Principles", SAFETY_REBRAND_PRINCIPLES_BODY: "We want to make sure that Discord has the ability for everyone to have a safe, positive and inclusive experience, no matter what brought them here. For that to happen, we must all agree to a set of rules that govern our interactions on Discord. When you sign up to Discord, you agree to follow the rules below and refrain from behavior that isn’t allowed on the service.\n\nIn exchange, it’s our job to make sure your experience is everything it can be. Here are the principles that guide the society we want to create on Discord:", SAFETY_REBRAND_PRINCIPLE_RESPONSIBILITY_TITLE: "We’re determined to make sure that Discord will always be a welcoming place for you.", SAFETY_REBRAND_PRINCIPLE_RESPONSIBILITY_SUBTITLE: "There’s a huge responsibility in being a place where hundreds of millions of people talk to each other.", SAFETY_REBRAND_PRINCIPLE_CONTROL_TITLE: "Privacy is incredibly important to us.", SAFETY_REBRAND_PRINCIPLE_CONTROL_SUBTITLE: "We do not monitor every server or every conversation. Moderators are at the forefront of creating spaces where people feel safe and can find belonging. Moderators are a key part of making communities great and a place where people want to gather.\n\nModeration takes hard work, and a commitment to learning more about how to make communities better. A key part of learning how to moderate comes simply from building and managing a community, but also from sharing knowledge learned by others sharing their insights on how to moderate communities more effectively.\n\nWe built the Discord Moderator Academy as a comprehensive resource so that anyone, from first-time moderators to experienced veterans of massive online communities, can find resources to learn about moderation, community management, and more.", MODACADEMY_CURRICULUM_TITLE: "The Curriculum", MODACADEMY_CURRICULUM_BODY: "The content of the Discord Moderator Academy is organized based on complexity.
